candidate_windows.window_text: In this section, we formalize the personalized dialogue response generation task and introduce our proposed RECAP method.

Our implementation is based on HuggingFace's Transformers (Wolf et al., 2020)12 and Sentence Transformer (Reimers and Gurevych, 2019) $^{13}$ codebases. We experiment with different settings and hyperparameters; the ones that work the best are discussed below. We initialize all encoders from the pre-trained RoBERTa-base model (Liu et al., 2019) $^{14}$ and initialize all decoders from the pre-trained DialogGPT-small model (Zhang et al., 2020b). RoBERTa's embedding dimension, $d$ , is 768, and $N$ , the prefix length, is set to 30 to align with the prompt length used in MSP. The two projection attentions in CAP are both single-head attentions. The number of history responses are 10, and for the models without a retrieval module (DialoGPT + history, DHAP, and CAP), the 10 most recent history responses are used. The utterance-level transformer has 768 hidden dimension, six layers, and a 12-head self-attention in each layer. We train all models using the AdamW optimizer (Loshchilov and Hutter, 2019) with learning rate 5e-5 and linear learning rate schedule for 10 epochs. The best models are chosen based on the validation perplexity. For generation, we use nucleus (top-p) sampling (Holtzman et al., 2020) with $p = 0.8$ . Table 1: Total number of parameters and training time (on $2\times$ A40 GPUs) for all neural models.
# ParamsTraining Time (hr)
DiaLoGPT124M8
DiaLoGPT + history124M37
DHAP431M25
MSP437M15
RE198M13
CAP269M22
All models including the baseline models are trained on $2 \times \mathrm{A40}$ GPUs with half precision training. The total number of parameters and training time are shown in Table 1. For MSP, the numbers are sums over all sub-modules (i.e. three refiners and DialogGPT generator). CAP includes both the context-aware prefix encoder and the DialogGPT generator.

The full automatic evaluation results are shown here in Table 8 and Table 9. Metrics within each category in Table 8 are overall consistent with each other. All token-overlap metrics and learning-based metrics are consistent with the human annotated fluency and coherency scores on the top two models. The style metrics are consistent with the human annotated style score on the top two models (with different order for CAV accuracy). Table 9 shows the full personal traits evaluation results. The metrics within each category are less consistent with each other, but the top two models on all metrics are always one of our four models, except for the MBTI J/P score.
